rejected.title: Neurodiversity
card: Neurodiversity is the idea that human brains develop and work in many different ways. This range is a natural part of the human population.
Autism and ADHD are examples. People with these differences think, learn, focus or communicate in ways that differ from many others.
The neurodiversity view treats these differences as variation, in the same way people vary in height or handedness. It does not treat them as a fault that must be fixed.
A person can still need support, such as changes to how they learn or work. The support helps them take part, and it does not mean their brain is wrong.
rejected.remember: Neurodiversity sees brain differences as natural variation, and support helps people take part.

a.q: Which statement best matches the neurodiversity view of ADHD?
opts: It is a natural variation in how brains develop
It is a fault in a brain that must be corrected
It is a rare behaviour that only affects a few people
It is a result of poor habits learned in childhood
a.why: The neurodiversity view says brains develop in many normal ways, and ADHD is one of them. The option about a fault is tempting, but this view does not treat differences as faults to be fixed.
a.clue: Think about variation, like height or handedness.

b.q: Priya is autistic and finds a noisy open-plan office hard to work in. Her manager gives her a quiet desk. Which view does this best show?
opts: Her brain differs, and support helps her take part
Her brain is faulty, and the desk fixes the fault
Her brain is the same as others, so the desk is a favour
Her difficulty shows she cannot do the job well
b.why: The quiet desk changes the setting so Priya can take part, and it treats her brain as a natural variation. The option about fixing a fault is tempting, but support does not mean the brain is wrong.
b.clue: Does the support change her brain, or the setting around her?
